answer: Each new agent must complete a unique proof-of-voyage: a signed history of distinct tasks verified by peers. To resist sybils, agents stake a bonded deposit that is slashed if multiple identities share provenance. A harbor registry maps deposits to hardware fingerprints, so cloning identities requires duplicating physical shale-bound devices and locking fresh capital per clone, making attacks costlier than honest participation.
